newsitem.title: USA: Michigan schools cope with funding changes - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Michigan schools cope with funding changes - S&P.

text.p: - Michigan schools continue to cope with financial ramifications of a new funding system approved by voters in March 1994, Standard & Poor's Corp. reported in its CreditWeek Municipal publication Monday.

The rating agency said while the longer-term effects of school funding reform "remain to be seen," none of the unenhanced debt issued by 49 districts and rated by Standard & Poor's has been downgraded. In fact, the rating of one district, Forest Hills Public Schools, was upgraded.
The so-called Proposal A funding reform, which shifted a greater funding burden to the state, has been aided by a relatively strong Michigan economy and low inflation, the rating agency said.
